components.note: Set-up (coordination, logic of sequences, straight rule and its three-part justification), syntax and semantics with the printed composite formulas, the four axioms (univocality, normalization, addition, multiplication) with the E-G glosses, Kolmogorov and sigma-field comparison (van Fraassen), the quoted rule of induction (1949 p.446) with n.8, the metalanguage status of the rule, the unstated joint syntax and iterated-implication semantics problem, posits (blind/appraised, Caesar n.9, atom decay), the flat-prior Bayes claim (n.10-11), pointwise versus uniform convergence, finite attainability, network of inductions (n.12), clairvoyant, non-uniqueness of convergent rules (n.13), pragmatic justification and the statistical-practice comparison are present and match the held text at the cited locators.

Chronology: 1915 thesis (principle of lawful distribution, weak LLN n.1), 1927 notes HR 044-06-21 with Hertz (nn.2-3), reversal of causality and probability, von Mises randomness versus normal sequences (n.4), finite segments and higher-order probability, hierarchical-Bayes comparison marked as E-G's device, reference classes (Maxwell/Bohr quotation, Mercury n.5), summary and 'at sea' verdict. Critics: Popper (two routes, regress, letter to Russell with 3/4 and 1/2), the 10% refutation and the 1949 p.436 reply, Nagel and Hertz, Creary's four conclusions (n.14), Tarski/Nagel extensionality (n.15), Russell's primes and finite-sequence proposal, Nagel's translation dilemma and the formal/applied reply. Rivals: Popper's asymmetry and the fruit vendor, Carnap/Hempel/Helmer-Oppenheim, Fisher and inverse probability, ravens, grue with the E-G rebuttal. Every stated theorem has written proof steps in the annex. Reichenbach's convergence theorems (1)-(4) and van Fraassen's result are explicitly not promoted to proofs (proofboundary, body 1259-1271).

Worked cases: gravitational-constant cross-induction (p-hat 0.8, 0.7, 0.79; q-hat 2/3), melting points, Caesar, Russell's primes, ravens, grue, noise-free line ax+b, the k-dataset p_f (n.16). Limitations and comparisons: aims (a)-(d), the three kinds of uncertainty, Jeffrey conditionalization, closing assessment and Notes on Sources with the 'remained at loss' qualification. Claim types are separated and each modern reconstruction (flat prior, Russell rearrangement, failure of contraposition) states its hypotheses; methodological claims are flagged as general observations.

duties.duty: The exact selected induction/confirmation source presentation must be authored; modern probability or a historical mention is not replacement source credit.
duties.note: The Eberhardt-Glymour chapter itself is reconstructed section by section (pp.357-387) with page locators; cross-references to sec:p15-reichenbach-probability-logic supplement but do not replace it.
